advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clean up the per-pid `.tmp` staging file (e.g. `staging.unlink(missing_ok=True)`) in the `finally` alongside the lock retire, so a failure between write and os.replace does not orphan it.
evidence: The `finally` at lines 160-168 only calls `lock.rmdir()`; it never unlinks `staging`.
advisory.finding: If the winner path fails between `staging.write_text(...)` and `os.replace(...)` (e.g. disk full, or an exception raised by write_text), the `finally` block retires the lock but the per-pid `.tmp` staging file is left behind; it is only ever removed as a side effect of a successful os.replace.
scenarios: A worker's write_text raises mid-fill (disk pressure) after creating the staging file
os.replace raises after the staging file is written
advisory.suggested_fix: In the finally block, add `staging.unlink(missing_ok=True)` (guarding the name binding) after attempting the lock rmdir.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the 150s-per-stratum worst-case wait on a crashed winner (documented as intentional) stays comfortably inside the 300s per-test timeout for every consumer, including the largest stratum.
evidence: 145-150: comment states the loser deliberately does NOT remove the lock even when the holder is gone
advisory.finding: If the winning worker's process is killed (not a Python exception) after `lock.mkdir()`, the lock directory is never removed for the rest of the session, so every other worker for that stratum blocks a full `_FILL_FALLBACK_SECONDS` (150s) before degrading to a local render — under -n 3 that serialises two workers on the dead stratum.
scenarios: A worker is OOM-killed or SIGKILLed mid-render while holding the lock directory
A winner hangs indefinitely on a pathological pandoc spawn

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test proving `_corpus_digest` changes (forcing a fresh render) when a rendering-relevant input other than `wiki_render.py`'s own bytes changes, or widen the digest to cover the renderer's transitive rendering inputs.
evidence: `digest.update(Path(wiki_render.__file__).read_bytes())` — only the single module file's bytes are hashed
`"""Pin the artifact to the inputs the render is a function of.` docstring claims coverage of 'the renderer source' but a renderer that delegates to imported helpers is not fully captured
Absence: the four safety consumers read from `corpus_pass1`; if the artifact is stale they assert against an obsolete render, so a real regression in an imported renderer helper would pass silently
Seeded-defect verification exists only as a manual ticket comment (20cb-cbae-e9df-45e3), not as a committed regression test
advisory.finding: The artifact digest (`_corpus_digest`) keys the cached pass-1 render only on `wiki_render.__file__`'s own bytes plus the corpus JSON and a pandoc stamp; it does not cover modules imported by `wiki_render` that affect its output. A behavior-changing edit to such a helper (leaving `wiki_render.py` bytes and the pandoc version/path/size unchanged) would serve a STALE artifact, and every safety test (protected excerpts, tables, HTML comments, coverage ratios) would then validate against an obsolete render instead of fresh pandoc output — regression blindness. No test asserts the digest actually invalidates when a rendering-relevant input changes.
scenarios: A rendering helper imported by wiki_render changes escaping behavior; wiki_render.py bytes and pandoc stamp are unchanged; the previous session's artifact is served and the safety tests validate against the pre-change render

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add direct tests for the shared-artifact helpers (digest invalidation, canonical ordering preservation across strata, loser-fallback local render) with a tmp root.
evidence: `_shared_stratum` / `_shared_pass1` are only referenced from within themselves and the fixture (search shows no test callers)
`pass1 = dict(corpus_pass1)` then `first = pass1[body]` at lines 282-284 assumes every `_load(stratum)` body is a key with no test guarding the mapping's completeness/ordering
Absence: no test drives `_shared_stratum` through the FileExistsError/deadline fallback branch or the os.replace publish branch
advisory.finding: The newly added cross-worker caching/concurrency machinery (`_corpus_digest`, `_probe_order`, `_shared_stratum` with its os.mkdir lock, deadline fallback, and os.replace publish, `_shared_pass1` canonical re-ordering) has no dedicated unit tests; it is exercised only implicitly via the `corpus_pass1` fixture. Its failure modes — loser-fallback local render, canonical body->render re-ordering across strata, digest-keyed filename — are not asserted, so a defect (e.g. `_shared_pass1` mis-ordering pairs, or `pass1[body]` KeyError on a missing body) would surface only as an unrelated downstream failure or not at all.
scenarios: `_shared_pass1`'s re-emit loop drops or mis-pairs a body under a partial-shard condition; the fixed-point test's `pass1[body]` raises KeyError or compares against the wrong render
